ei.title: The Need to Suppress Persistent Old Theories in Conceptual Learning

fullPassage: How do children learn new concepts? The traditional view of conceptual change was that new learned theories replace old ones: once a child learns that the Earth rotates around the sun, their previous theory, based on their experience of seeing the sun move, that the sun rotates around the Earth, would be overwritten. Recent evidence from adults suggests something more surprising: that these old, incorrect theories remain stored in the brain; often we still need them to drive our perceptual expectations such as where to look for the sun in the sky. But in an educational context, we need inhibitory control to suppress them in order to reach the newer, correct theories. The naive incorrect theory is more familiar and automatic; the new theory needs time and deliberate suppression of the old theory to be actively retrieved.

det.korean: accidental(우연한) → deliberate(의도적인).

det.tip: deliberate(의도적인) ↔ accidental(우연한). 새 이론 인출에는 의도적 노력 필요.

det.analysis: 원문 'we need inhibitory control to suppress them'에서 inhibitory가 정답.
det.tip: inhibitory = 억제적인. inhibit(억제하다) → inhibitory(형용사).

questions.passage: How do children learn new concepts? The traditional view of conceptual change was that new learned theories replace old ones: once a child learns that the Earth rotates around the sun, their previous theory, based on their experience of seeing the sun move, that the sun rotates around the Earth, would be overwritten. __________ that these old, incorrect theories remain stored in the brain; often we still need them to drive our perceptual expectations such as where to look for the sun in the sky. But in an educational context, we need inhibitory control to suppress them in order to reach the newer, correct theories. The naive incorrect theory is more familiar and automatic; the new theory needs time and deliberate suppression of the old theory to be actively retrieved.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어들을 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)

[ Recent / evidence / from / adults / suggests / something / more / surprising ] (8단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 성인 대상 최근 증거는 더 놀라운 것을 시사한다.
det.analysis: Recent evidence(주어) + from adults(수식어) + suggests(동사) + something more surprising(목적어).
det.tip: evidence suggests = 증거가 시사하다. something + 형용사(more surprising).

questions.passage: How do children learn new concepts? The traditional view of conceptual change was that new learned theories replace old ones: once a child learns that the Earth rotates around the sun, their previous theory, based on their experience of seeing the sun move, that the sun rotates around the Earth, would be overwritten. Recent evidence from adults suggests something more surprising: that these old, incorrect theories remain stored in the brain; often we still need them to drive our perceptual expectations such as where to look for the sun in the sky. But in an educational context, we need inhibitory control to suppress them in order to reach the newer, correct theories. The naive incorrect theory is more familiar and automatic; the new theory needs time and deliberate suppression of the old theory to be actively retrieved.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 개념 학습에서 옛 이론의 지속성과 억제 필요성.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 개념 학습에서 옛 이론의 지속성과 억제 필요성: 옛 이론이 뇌에 남아있어 억제가 필요하다는 글 전체.
❌ ① 태양계의 과학적 발견: 태양 예시일 뿐 전체 주제 아님.
❌ ③ 아동 교육의 역사적 변천: 역사적 변천이 아님.
❌ ④ 성인과 아동의 뇌 구조 차이: 뇌 구조 차이가 주제 아님.
det.tip: 주제 = 옛 이론의 지속성 + 억제 필요성.

questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어, '덮어쓰이다'의 의미)

det.korean: 이전 이론이 덮어쓰인다(overwritten)는 전통적 견해.
det.analysis: 원문 'would be overwritten'에서 overwritten이 정답.
det.tip: overwrite(덮어쓰다) → overwritten(과거분사). 이전 것이 새 것으로 대체됨.
